— Pavement markings, lanes, toll, curbs","learner_facing":true,"markdown":"## C — Pavement markings, lanes, toll, curbs

FACT_ID: sec05-F01 | anchor: A01
A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line allows passing only from the broken side; solid-side drivers may cross only for pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear and safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F02 | anchor: A01
Double solid yellow lines mark the road center between opposing flows: no passing either way, crossing only for left turns or for pedestrians, bicyclists, or scooter and skateboard riders when the opposite lane is clear and safe [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F03 | anchor: A01
Broken white lines divide same-direction lanes: change lanes with caution [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F04 | anchor: A01
Dotted white lines assign lanes through intersections and interchanges, guide paired turning lanes, and mark turn-lane openings and entrance and exit lanes [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F05 | anchor: A01
On an unmarked two-lane road, you may pass a slow vehicle on the left where no signs prohibit passing and the way is clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F06 | anchor: A01
Portable and permanent message boards report traffic, road, and weather hazards: always obey their directions [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F07 | anchor: A01
Rumble strip warnings mean driving slowly straight over the strips, never swerving around them [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F08 | anchor: A01
Slow moving vehicles at 25 MPH or less, such as farm equipment, horse-drawn vehicles, and work vehicles, display warning signs; adjust your speed or position for them [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F09 | anchor: A01
Road markings guide, warn, and regulate traffic in red, yellow, or white, used alone or combined [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F10 | anchor: A01
Red markings are rare, though some towns use red curbs for no parking; red pavement reflectors face wrong-way traffic only [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F11 | anchor: A01
Yellow center lines mean two-way opposite-direction traffic, and a broken yellow center allows passing on the left in either direction when ahead is clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec05-F12 | anchor: A02
A yield line of triangles across the road, often with a yield sign or at a roundabout entrance, marks where to yield or stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F13 | anchor: A02
On three-lane two-way roads, the marked center lane serves left turns or passing [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F14 | anchor: A02
A center lane with a broken yellow line on both sides is open to passing from either direction [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F15 | anchor: A02
A center lane with solid plus broken yellow on both sides is open to left turns from either direction, but never to more than 150 feet of travel [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F16 | anchor: A02
A sharrow pairs a bicycle symbol with a double chevron on lanes too narrow to share side by side: bicyclists ride there and drivers expect them [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F17 | anchor: A02
Bicycle lanes marked by solid or dashed white lines or green pavement with a bike symbol stay preferential for bikes; drivers enter only to turn, after mirror checks and yielding to lane bikes [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F18 | anchor: A02
Solid white lines mark turn lanes and the right pavement edge, discourage changes near intersections and ramps, and pair with arrows that dictate the allowed turn; stop lines, crosswalks, and parking spaces also use white [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F19 | anchor: A02
A curved arrow alone or with ONLY means you must turn that way, while a curved plus straight arrow means you may turn or go straight [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F20 | anchor: A02
Wrong-way arrows mean you are driving against traffic toward a head-on crash: slow down and pull over at once [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F21 | anchor: A02
Double solid white lines divide same-direction lanes, often shielding special-use lanes like HOV lanes: never cross them, entering only where signs and markings allow [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0014]

FACT_ID: sec05-F22 | anchor: A03
Bicycle boxes at intersections hold waiting riders ahead of drivers: stop behind the box on red, never inside it, make no right on red there, and on green signal right turns while yielding to bikes on the right [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F23 | anchor: A03
Bus-only lanes carry BUS ONLY markings, red-colored pavement, or both [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F24 | anchor: A03
HOV lanes carry center diamonds and may run barrier-separated or behind double white lines; in heavy traffic they serve buses, vanpools, carpools, high-occupancy vehicles, motorcycles, and certain clean-fuel vehicles, with signs posting minimum passengers and hours, and barrier lanes reverse direction by time of day [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F25 | anchor: A03
A diamond marking can also reserve a lane for buses [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F26 | anchor: A03
Every Virginia toll facility accepts E-ZPass transponders: follow purple-logo lanes with one, cash lanes without one, slowing with caution for lane changers and crossing employees [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F27 | anchor: A03
High-speed E-ZPass lanes are transponder-only; a mistaken entry must never stop, since cameras photograph the plate and bill the registered owner [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]

FACT_ID: sec05-F28 | anchor: A03
Painted curbs set parking rules to confirm with the locality: white allows only passenger pickup and dropoff, yellow allows only loading with the driver staying, and red bans stopping, standing, and parking [A03].
Source: [A03 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0015]
